description: Helps you decide how to turn a customer result into a case study, a post and a newsletter while preserving its exact sentence. Needs the exact result sentence with its qualifier and source label, source and date, your role, approval, your own view and a reader action. Returns a proof card, first drafts and a sentence check. Optional proof details expose gaps. Written approval is required for your own customer; without it, returns the card and questions only. Chat collects the facts; the results view shows them. No form. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing or invalid brief fields return field-specific errors. Missing written approval for your own customer returns the proof card and questions only. Use this instead of case_study_generator when you need a proof card and several drafts preserving one exact result sentence.

approval.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"status":"written","approver":"finance director","date":"2026-11-17","uses":["case study"]}.

approver.description: Who approved the uses, in writing. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

date.description: Approval date as year, month and day. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

status.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "written".

uses.description: Every use explicitly covered by the written approval. Format is a JSON array. For example, ["case study"].

items.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "case study".

as_of_date.description: The date of this run as year, month and day. Supplied by chat so repeats stay identical. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

buyer_role.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "vendor".

buyer_view.description: Your own view in whole sentences. The tool will not invent it. Format is text. For example, "Finance teams need a clear owner for each invoice exception.".

call_to_action.description: One action you want the reader to take. Format is text. For example, "book a discovery call".

challenge.description: The customer problem from the approved story. Format is text. For example, "invoice exceptions delay month-end close".

customer_name.description: Customer label, including an approved anonymous description. Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

exact_sentence.description: Copy the result exactly, keeping its qualifier and source label inside this sentence. Format is text. For example, "Company-reported pilot reduced approval time from 12 to 9 days in October 2026.".

headline.description: Your own headline, if available. Format is text. For example, "Reducing invoice approval delays".

measured_result.description: False for a story with no measured outcome. Never infer an improvement from exposure or scale counts. Format is true or false. For example, true.

product.description: Your product or vendor name. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

proof_details.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"qualifier":"in the measured pilot","counted":"120 eligible invoices","definition":"days from invoice receipt to approval"}.

before.description: The before figure. Format is text. For example, "12 days".

counted.description: What was counted. Format is text. For example, "120 eligible invoices".

definition.description: What counts as the outcome. Format is text. For example, "days from invoice receipt to approval".

denominator.description: Out of how many eligible cases. Format is text. For example, "120 eligible invoices".

fell_out.description: How excluded or abandoned cases were counted. Format is text. For example, "cancelled invoices excluded from both periods".

period.description: The measurement period. Format is text. For example, "October 2026".

qualifier.description: The qualifier inside the locked sentence, or none stated. Format is text. For example, "in the measured pilot".

reporter.description: Who reported the result. Format is text. For example, "finance director".

review_by.description: Review date as year, month and day. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

published_story.description: The already published story as plain text. Used as source without rebuilding it. Format is text. For example, "Invoice exceptions delay close. Review unresolved exceptions weekly with finance.".

relationship.description: Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "own_customer".

solution.description: What was done, from the approved story. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

source_checked_date.description: The date you reopened the source, as year, month and day. This is not the publication date. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-11-17".

source_date.description: Publication or evidence date as year, month and day, or not stated. Keep it separate from the measurement period. Format is text in YYYY-MM-DD form. For example, "2026-10-31".

source_kind.description: Who stands behind the result. A company report is not independent evidence. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "company_reported".

source_label.description: The source label already inside the exact sentence, for example company-reported. Format is text.

source_url.description: Public source or approved evidence link, using https. Format is text. For example, "https://example.org/approved-evidence".

story_published.description: Format is true or false. For example, true.

name: customer_result_to_content
title: Turn this customer result into content
